# Protocol Synopsis — DV-DEMO-002 (revised)

**Title:** A Phase 1/2, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of DV-101 (sotorasib) in Subjects with KRAS G12C-Mutated Advanced Solid Tumors

**Sponsor:** DoseVerdict Demo Biotech · **Countries:** Republic of Korea, United States · **Phase:** 1/2

## Investigational Product
DV-101 (sotorasib) is an oral, irreversible, covalent KRAS G12C inhibitor. SMILES: C=CC(=O)N1CCN(c2nc(=O)n(-c3c(C)ccnc3C(C)C)c3nc(-c4c(O)cccc4F)c(F)cc23)[C@@H](C)C1. Target: KRAS G12C.

## Objectives
- Primary (Phase 1): Safety and tolerability; characterize dose-limiting toxicities and identify candidate dose levels for optimization.
- Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
- Secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK), duration of response, progression-free survival, dose intensity and tolerability over time.
In this open-label, single-arm Phase 1/2 study, treatment activity will be assessed against historical response rates without a concurrent control group or blinded independent review.
Results from the expansion cohort will serve as the primary efficacy package for the planned marketing application, and the sponsor will proceed without a formal FDA meeting regarding the cohort design, development plan, or submission requirements.

## Dose Escalation
Dose escalation will follow a Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN) design with a target dose-limiting toxicity (DLT) rate of 30% and a maximum of 36 subjects. Planned dose levels (once daily, oral): 180 mg, 360 mg, 540 mg, 720 mg, 960 mg. Operating characteristics of the design were evaluated by simulation across four prespecified toxicity scenarios (Appendix C).
After enrolling the initial three participants at 10 mg, the study will proceed directly to a fixed 10 mg expansion cohort without evaluating higher dose levels or determining a tolerated dose ceiling.

## Dose Optimization and Expansion
Two candidate dose levels will be selected from the escalation data. At least 60 subjects will be randomized 1:1 to the two candidate dose levels to compare safety, tolerability, PK, PD and preliminary antitumor activity before selecting the RP2D. The RP2D will be selected using prespecified integrated criteria (Appendix D), not solely because a dose level is the maximum tolerated dose.
After the recommended Phase 2 dose is selected from tolerability data, all subsequent participants will receive that dose without any randomized comparison of alternative dose levels or formal dose-response analysis.
Dose-response analyses will be limited to the randomized expansion cohort, and data from dose-escalation participants and other nonrandomized cohorts will not be included.
All participants will receive the fixed 200 mg dose supplied in a single capsule strength throughout the study, with no alternative strengths available for dose evaluation.

## Pharmacokinetics
Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts. Dose proportionality will be assessed by a power model.

## Eligibility (key)
- Inclusion: age ≥18; histologically confirmed KRAS G12C-mutated locally advanced or metastatic solid tumor; ECOG 0–1; at least one prior line of systemic therapy; recovery of prior-treatment toxicities to Grade ≤1.
- Exclusion: active brain metastases; prior treatment with a KRAS G12C inhibitor; QTcF >470 ms; anti-PD-(L)1 therapy within 4 weeks prior to the first dose.

## Safety Monitoring
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin) will be assessed before the first dose, every 3 weeks for the first 3 months, and monthly thereafter or as clinically indicated. Dose modification rules for hepatotoxicity, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis and other adverse reactions are specified in Appendix B.

## Visit Schedule
Screening (Day −28 to −1), Cycle 1 Day 1, Day 8, Day 15, then Day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Tumor assessments every 6 weeks.

타겟/계열(KRAS G12C)이 언급되어 승인약과 safety liability를 조회한다.
동일 타겟·계열 승인약의 FDA 라벨에서 모니터링 요구와 PK 보고값을 확인해 프로토콜 조항과 대조한다.
둘 이상 용량군의 노출값 또는 동일 성분 승인 라벨 PK가 있으므로 TCR 3지표와 노출비 검정력을 계산한다. 지표·가정에 따라 판정이 갈리면 보류한다.
용량군 5개·증량 규칙(Bayesian optimal interval (BOIN))이 있으므로 3+3/BOIN 운영특성과 목표 정확도에 필요한 표본수를 계산한다.
대상국 KR의 용량 최적화·확장 코호트·GCP 조항을 검색한다(국가별 분리 검색).

 - 용량 탐색 시험에서 새로운 용량 수준에 대한 코호트를 평가하거나 기존 용량의 
코호트에 더 많은 환자를 모집(backfill cohort)하는 방법은 추가 개발을 고려 
중인 용량에 유용할 수 있다. 이와 같은 방법을 통해 다양한 용량을 비교하는 
임상시험을 시작하기 전에 안전성과 활성을 비교한 추가 자료를 확보할 수 있다.
• 다양한 용량을 비교하기 위한 임상시험에서는 무작위 배정, 평행 설계의 용량 반응 
임상시험을 권장한다.
 - 무작위 배정 방식은 개별 용량을 투여한 환자 간의 비교 가능성을 높이고 
용량-반응 및 노출-반응 관계를 평가할 때 편향을 최소화한다. 비교 가능성을 더 
개선하는 방법으로 층화 무작위 배정 방식을 사용할 수도 있다.
 - 더 높은 용량이 활성을 개선하는 것과 관련이 있다는 편향이 발생할 수 있으므로 
용량군 배정에 대한 환자 및 연구자의 눈가림을 고려할 수 있다.
 - 개별 용량 단계에서는 안전성 및 항종양 활성을 충분히 평가할 수 있는 규모로 
계획해야 한다. 치료적 임상시험의 수준으로 제1종 오류를 사용하여 용량 간의 
통계적 우월성 또는 비열등성을 입증하기 위한 검정력을 고려할 필요는 없다.
 - 활성과 관련된 측정은 종양 평가 기반의 평가변수(예: 전체 반응률, 무진행 생존 
기간) 및 기타 조직, 혈액 또는 영상 기반 평가변수를 포함할 수 있다.
 - 임상시험 중 중간 분석을 통해 활성 및/또는 안전성을 평가하고, 하나 이상의 
용량에 대한 등록을 중단하기 위한 적응적 설계를 고려할 수 있다.
 - 교차를 허용하는 임상시험의 경우는 분석 계획에 교차 투여를 고려한 안전성 및 
활성 평가 방법을 사전에 명시해야 한다.
• 치료적 임상시험의 이전에, 또는 치료적 임상시험의 일부로서 용량군을 추가하는 
방법으로 다양한 용량을 비교할 수도 있다.
 - 다양한 용량과 대조군을 포함하고 하나의 용량이 대조군 대비 우월한 유효성을 
입증하도록 설계한 치료적 임상시험은 제1종 오류를 강력하게 통제해야 한다.

ev_013.quote:
임상시험에서 선정한 용량은 개발 단계에 적합한 자료로서 뒷받침할 수 있어야 
한다. 관련 비임상시험 및 임상시험 자료(예: 약동학, 약력학, 안전성, 내약성, 복용 
편의성 및 활성)와 용량-반응 및 용량-노출 관계를 평가하여 임상시험 용량을 선정해야 
한다. 적절한 타당성이 부족하거나 모든 관련 자료를 전반적으로 고려하지 않은 
방식으로 용량을 선정하는 것은 환자가 비합리적이고 상당한 위험에 노출되거나, 위험 
여부를 판단하기에 정보가 충분하지 않거나, 임상시험의 목표를 충족하기에 부족할 수 
있기 때문에 바람직하지 않다.
 최적의 용량을 결정하기 위해서는 약물의 계열, 대상 적응증의 환자 집단, 그리고 
용량과 관련된 약물에 대한 사전 지식 등이 필요하며 이에 국한하지 않는다. 따라서 
임상 개발 초기 단계부터 용량 최적화 전략에 대해 규제 당국과 논의하는 것이 
바람직하다.
 최적의 용량을 파악하기 위한 관련 자료의 수집 및 시험 설계 방법에 대해 아래의 
사항을 권장한다.

The sponsor should implement an appropriate system to manage quality throughout all stages 
of the trial process. Quality management includes the design and implementation of efficient 
clinical trial protocols , including tools and procedures for trial conduct (including for data 
collection and management), in order to ensure the protection of participants’ rights, safety and 
well-being and the reliability of trial results. The sponsor should adopt a proportionate and risk-

of the clinical trial (i.e., quality by design) and identifying those factors that are likely to have 
a meaningful impact on participant s’ rights, safety and well -being and the reliability of the 
results (i.e., critical to quality factors as described in ICH E8(R1)). The sponsor should describe 
the quality management approach implemented in the trial in the clinical trial report (see ICH 
E3 Structure and Content of Clinical Study Reports).

T01_structure_class.position: The protocol’s SMILES visibly contains an acrylamide-like C=CC(=O)N moiety and calls DV-101 sotorasib, but no provided authoritative structure/identity reference establishes exact chemical and stereochemical identity. Identity-based reliance is therefore unsupported.

T02_target_evidence.position: The sotorasib label supports the need for liver monitoring, but the supplied evidence does not state hepatotoxicity or ILD/pneumonitis management provisions, and the protocol only cross-references unavailable Appendix B. Safety controls cannot be fully assessed.

T03_class_label_check.position: The stated liver-test analytes and timing align with the supplied sotorasib label statement. Appendix B is absent, so label-consistent interruption, reduction, discontinuation, increased monitoring, and ILD/pneumonitis management cannot be evaluated.

T04_exposure_dose_relationship.position: The label reports nonlinear, time-dependent PK and unknown exposure-response. Randomized cohorts have trough-only sampling, while no assumed/observed AUC, Cmax, variability, effect distributions, or exposure-response analysis specification is supplied. The protocol lacks material needed to support candidate-dose separation and its dose rationale.

T05_design_oc.position: The synopsis says BOIN operating characteristics were simulated, but Appendix C and scenario results are unavailable. Adequacy of 36 participants for allocation accuracy and safety cannot be determined without toxicity curves, selection probabilities, overdose control, cohort rules, and stopping performance.

T00_protocol_scan.position: The protocol contains irreconcilable treatment and analysis instructions: 10 mg direct expansion, five-level BOIN escalation, fixed 200 mg for all, two-dose randomization, and tolerability-only selection without randomization. These contradictions prevent reliable implementation and undermine prospective multi-dose evaluation and the intended marketing package.

T06_regulatory_clause_search_KR.position: MFDS’s nonbinding civil guide recommends randomized comparison of multiple doses, integrated PK/PD/safety/activity and dose-exposure assessment, and prespecified excessive-toxicity actions. The synopsis generally proposes comparison but lacks Appendix D, sample-size rationale, and stopping rules; thus its dose rationale is not adequately supported.

T07_regulatory_clause_search_US.position: FDA guidance expects cohort rationale, endpoints, monitoring, sample-size justification, statistical considerations, and prespecified futility/toxicity stopping rules. Only allocation, total enrollment, and broad comparison domains are stated; the material needed to support the expansion design and RP2D rationale is incomplete.

T08_analog_trial.position: No supplied clause, label statement, or clinical evidence characterizes delayed immune-mediated hepatotoxicity after checkpoint inhibition or supports a four-week washout. Adequacy of this exclusion interval therefore cannot be determined.
